subject.title: Feature: Auto session split when approaching context window limit

question: Should OpenClaw add a core context-pressure session rollover policy, and if so what public config, defaults, handoff artifact, privacy, and delivery-preservation contract should it use?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but implementing it adds new public session lifecycle config and persistent handoff semantics that affect compatibility, privacy, channel routing, and existing reset/compaction behavior.

options.title: Design Core Rollover Policy First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the canonical session.context rollover shape, disabled-by-default behavior, handoff storage, authorization, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into General Session TTL Policy
options.body: Treat token-pressure rollover as part of a broader session lifecycle policy with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45390, accepting a larger but more unified design pass.

options.title: Decline Automatic Rollover
options.body: Keep compaction, memory flush, and manual/daily/idle reset as the supported controls and close this cluster after documenting that product direction.

recommendation.title: Design Core Rollover Policy First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the canonical session.context rollover shape, disabled-by-default behavior, handoff storage, authorization, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced daily reset and pre-compaction memory flush, the closest core lifecycle behaviors that the requested policy would extend.
